# Paradise OS UI

> Seven vaporwave UI controls built out of photographed 1995 parts: a holographic CD you turn to change songs, an equalizer of pool water in a pink ceramic rack, a slider that floods a tiled pool, a switch between paradise and reality, an error dialog that cascades, three floating CRT monitors as tabs, and a marble bust that shows what an AI agent is doing. Each is one plain script that registers a custom element, with its photographed parts and fonts inside it: no dependencies, no build step. MIT licensed.

Live gallery: https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app
Source: https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui

## Drop-in components

Each is one plain script that registers a custom element. Load it with a script tag, not as a module. Do not rewrite or split the file. Each carries a copy of the shared core; the first one loaded sets window.ParadiseOS and window.ParadiseSound and the rest reuse them, so any mix shares one clock, one sound engine and one bus.

- [CD-ROM jukebox](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/cd-dial/cd-dial.js): A holographic CD on a marble platter that is a five-track music player. Turn the disc and it clicks from track to track, the laser arm seeks across the grooves and the song changes; click the hub to play or pause. Use <paradise-cd-dial tracks="audio/"></paradise-cd-dial>. Read el.track (0 to 4) and el.playing; it fires input while it turns, change when it settles and track-change when the track changes. Give it tracks="folder/" holding trk-01.mp3 to trk-05.mp3 for real songs; without that each track is a beat synthesized on the spot. Draws at 268 × 244 px. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/blob/main/cd-dial/README.md)
- [Equalizer](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/eq/eq.js): A seven-band equalizer: seven slots in a glazed pink ceramic rack, each filled with pool water and topped with a chrome pearl. Swipe across the slots to sculpt the curve; while music plays the water dances to it and the pearls hold the peaks. Use <paradise-eq preset="mallsoft"></paradise-eq>. Read el.getValues() (seven whole numbers from 0 to 100); it fires input while you paint and change when you let go. preset picks a starting curve. Draws at 444 × 236 px. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/blob/main/eq/README.md)
- [Pool slider](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/slider/slider.js): A range slider drawn as a pink-tiled pool with a checkerboard floor. The value is how full it is: drag the chrome ball and the water floods after it in real waves; flick it and the water slops; over 85% it overflows. Use <paradise-pool-slider value="62"></paradise-pool-slider>. Read el.value (0 to 100); it fires input while it moves and change when it is let go. With a name it is sent with its form. Draws at 560 × 225 px. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/blob/main/slider/README.md)
- [Dream toggle](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/toggle/toggle.js): A switch in a little 95-era dialog window. On, the track is pool water and the label says DREAM ON; drag the knob and water leaks across before it snaps. Off, every Paradise control on the page drops to grey wireframe reality. Use <paradise-toggle checked></paradise-toggle>. Read el.checked; it fires change. With a name it is sent with its form when on. mode="busy" or "locked" stops it. Draws at 244 × 98 px. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/blob/main/toggle/README.md)
- [Cascade button](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/button/button.js): A button drawn as a 95-era error dialog. Click it and a few copies of the dialog cascade down and bounce like dealt cards; hold it and a wireframe hypercube unfolds inside, and letting go fires a cascade as big as the charge. Use <paradise-cascade-button label="Still dreaming?"></paradise-cascade-button>. Listen for action (detail.combo, detail.mega); charge fires while it is held, with detail.charge from 0 to 1. Draws at 248 × 110 px. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/blob/main/button/README.md)
- [CRT tabs](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/tabs/tabs.js): Three little beige CRT monitors hanging at different heights. Click one and it powers on to its channel (a pool, a sunset, an aquarium) while the others collapse to a dot; double-click to degauss it. Use <paradise-crt-tabs value="1"></paradise-crt-tabs>. Read el.value (0, 1 or 2); it fires change with detail.channel. select(i) switches from code; degauss() wobbles the picture. Draws at 499 × 266 px. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/blob/main/tabs/README.md)
- [Statue agent status](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/agent-status/agent-status.js): A status indicator for an AI agent: a marble bust floating over a checkerboard plinth, drawn in 3D. Each state looks different: thinking splits it into turning slabs, searching scans it with a laser, writing sends glyphs up, error cracks it red, done slams it into a pool of light. Use <paradise-statue state="thinking"></paradise-statue>. Set el.state to idle, thinking, searching, tool, writing, error or done; el.progress (0 to 1) draws a ring. pulse() fires one burst. Draws at 240 × 256 px. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/blob/main/agent-status/README.md)

Install any one with the shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn add finktheartist/paradise-os-ui/NAME`, where NAME is cd-dial, eq, slider, toggle, button, tabs, agent-status. The file lands in `public/paradise-os-ui/`.

Each draws at a fixed size on a light page and makes small synthesized sounds after the first tap (ParadiseSound.muted = true silences them). The CD dial's five songs are separate files in https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/audio/ (trk-01.mp3 to trk-05.mp3); point its tracks attribute at a folder holding them.

## The skill

- [paradise-os-ui skill](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/skills/paradise-os-ui/SKILL.md): the workflow and rules these were made by. Install with `npx skills add finktheartist/paradise-os-ui`.
- [core.js](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/skills/paradise-os-ui/core.js): the shared core (clock, springs, element base class, bus, drawing helpers, fonts) with the sound engine.
- [starter.html](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/skills/paradise-os-ui/starter.html): the smallest whole example, a new control built on the core.
- [look.mjs](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/skills/paradise-os-ui/look.mjs): stops the clock, steps an interaction to chosen moments and saves the frames side by side.

## How they were made

- [making-of/README.md](https://paradise-os-ui.vercel.app/making-of/README.md): how the set was made, and every prompt used for its pictures and songs.
